title: AI supporting PRINCE2 Agile
blurb: Recognize how AI can support the PRINCE2 Agile principles, people and practices, while people keep the decisions and the data is handled with care.
question: A project manager wants to use AI to forecast whether the expected benefits still fit the budget and timeline. Which principle does this support, and what must stay with people?

teach.h: AI as an assistant, not a decision-maker
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile describes how AI can support its principles and its people element, and through them the practices and artifacts used every day. AI can forecast, analyse, draft, prioritize and automate routine information flows. It supports, but does not remove, human decision-making or the need to talk with stakeholders: the defined roles stay accountable.

teach.h: How AI can support the principles
head: Principle
AI support
rows: Predictive analytics on viability; early warning of overruns
Suggests role assignments; flags gaps or overlaps
Adjusts time, cost, benefit forecasts; refines next plans
Defines and breaks down products; drafts stories; automated testing
Spots similar past projects; suggests tailoring
teach.caption: Paraphrased from 15.4.1.

teach.body: For leading teams, AI can help people understand team relationships, individual strengths and how workload is spread. For communication, it can automate the collection and sharing of information, give timely insights, add transparency and answer common questions through a project chatbot. That frees leaders for strategic, high-impact conversations; it does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders.

teach.h: AI in the practices and artifacts
teach.body: In everyday practice that might mean forecasting benefits against the project canvas (business case), suggesting role assignments (organization), refining the next iteration or stage plan and the release map (plans), drafting user stories and prioritizing backlogs, automated testing against acceptance criteria (quality) and early warnings of cost overruns (risk and progress). PeopleCert guidance adds examples such as summarizing retrospective themes or spotting patterns in team dashboard data.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1; PeopleCert white paper on AI for PRINCE2 Agile (2026)

teach.body: AI is only as reliable as the data it uses, so check that backlogs, dashboards, risks and lessons are current before trusting its output, and treat that output as a draft to review. Be open about AI use: the digital and data management approach describes how data is created, used and kept secure, including privacy, which matters when AI processes personal data or retrospective comments.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 7 manual (digital and data management approach); PeopleCert white paper on AI for PRINCE2 Agile (2026)

teach.body: At Kingsfold Engineering, project manager Daniel Kim uses an AI tool that forecasts, from real-time cost data, that benefits may slip behind budget; he brings the forecast to executive Sara Lund, who decides. Product owner Ayesha Rahman uses AI to draft user stories, then refines them with her team. Agile coach Maria Rossi adds a note to the digital and data management approach on how retrospective comments are anonymized before any AI analysis.

teach.text: AI supports decisions; it does NOT take them, and it does NOT remove the need to communicate with stakeholders. A project chatbot handles common questions so leaders have more time for strategic conversations, not less contact.

items: Business justification: predictive analytics forecasts viability and warns of overruns.
Learn from experience: lessons made searchable and prioritized.
Defined roles: role suggestions; gaps and overlaps flagged.
Manage by stages and focus on products: refined forecasts, drafted stories, automated testing.
People: insight into relationships, strengths, workload; automated information, FAQ chatbot.
Humans decide and communicate; data handled under the digital and data management approach.

summary: You can now recognize how AI can support each PRINCE2 Agile principle, the people element and everyday practices. You also know that people keep the decisions and that AI use relies on good, well-managed data.

A.q: How can AI support the principle 'ensure continued business justification'?
options: By generating the project mandate from past projects
By forecasting viability from historical and real-time data
By taking the project board's investment decisions
By automating the creative design of products
A.why: Predictive analytics can forecast whether expected benefits still align with timelines and budgets and warn of overruns (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: The mandate comes from the business layer that commissions the project.
whyNot.2: AI supports decisions; the board still takes them.
whyNot.3: The book links this principle to forecasting viability, not creative tasks.

A.q: Which principle does AI support by turning large volumes of lessons into searchable, prioritized, role-specific insights?
options: Manage by stages
Focus on products
Learn from experience
Defined roles
A.why: AI helps lessons actually get used by making them accessible and actionable (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Manage by stages is supported by refined forecasts for the next stage.
whyNot.1: Focus on products is supported by defining products and drafting stories.
whyNot.3: Defined roles is supported by role suggestions and gap analysis.

A.q: How can AI support effective communication in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
options: By automating the collection and sharing of information
By sending every stakeholder message in place of leaders
By deciding which stakeholders need to be informed
By replacing the communication management approach
A.why: AI can automate collecting and sharing information, giving timely insights and transparency, so leaders can focus on strategic communication (15.4.2).

whyNot.1: Leaders still communicate; AI frees time for high-impact conversations.
whyNot.2: Deciding who to inform remains a human judgement in the communication approach.
whyNot.3: AI supports the approach; it does not replace it.

B.q: AI analyses project data, skills and workload to suggest role assignments and flag gaps or overlaps in responsibilities. Which principle does this support?
options: Learn from experience
Tailor to suit the project
Focus on products
Defined roles
B.why: This is how AI supports defined roles and responsibilities (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience is supported by making lessons accessible.
whyNot.1: Tailoring is supported by comparing with similar past projects.
whyNot.2: Focus on products is supported by product definition and testing.

B.q: Which statement about AI and decision-making in PRINCE2 Agile is correct?
options: AI supports decisions, and people stay responsible for them
AI should take routine board decisions to save time
AI removes the need for conversations with stakeholders
AI output can be approved unreviewed once it has proved accurate
B.why: AI supports but does not remove human decision-making or the need to communicate with stakeholders (15.4.2).

whyNot.1: Board decisions stay with the board.
whyNot.2: Communication with stakeholders is still needed.
whyNot.3: Output still needs review by the accountable role each time.

B.q: Which principle does AI support by spotting similarities with past projects and suggesting where agile practices fit best?
options: Learn from experience
Manage by stages
Tailor to suit the project
Ensure continued business justification
B.why: AI supports tailoring by comparing with past projects and suggesting adaptations (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience is about making lessons searchable and actionable.
whyNot.1: Manage by stages is about adjusting forecasts and next plans.
whyNot.3: Business justification is about forecasting viability.

C.q:
Which two statements about AI in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. AI can help draft user stories and prioritize backlogs.
2. A project chatbot can answer stakeholders' common questions.
3. AI removes the need for leaders to communicate with stakeholders.
4. AI-powered testing replaces the Definition of Done.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
C.why: AI can draft stories and prioritize backlogs (15.4.1), and a project chatbot can answer FAQs (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is wrong: communication with stakeholders is still needed.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: automated tests check products against criteria such as the DoD; they do not replace it.

C.q: AI adjusts forecasts of time, cost and benefits from current progress and refines the plan for the next stage. Which principle does this support, and which artifact is MOST LIKELY updated?
options: Focus on products; the product backlog
Defined roles; the skill matrix
Learn from experience; the lessons log
Manage by stages; the release map
C.why: Refining time, cost and benefit forecasts and next stage plans supports manage by stages (15.4.1); in agile the stage plan is the release map.

whyNot.0: Focus on products is about defining products and stories.
whyNot.1: Defined roles is about role assignments.
whyNot.2: Learn from experience is about lessons, not forecasts.

C.q: Which management product describes how project data, including personal data processed by AI tools, will be created, used, kept secure and managed?
options: Digital and data management approach
Communication management approach
Quality management approach
Risk management approach
C.why: The digital and data management approach describes how data is created, used and managed, including security and privacy (PRINCE2 7 progress practice; PRINCE2 Agile book ch 12).

whyNot.1: The communication approach covers how and when stakeholders are informed.
whyNot.2: The quality approach covers quality methods and responsibilities.
whyNot.3: The risk approach covers the risk procedure; data handling has its own approach.

reteach.title: A sat nav on a long drive
reteach.question: How is AI on a project like a sat nav on a long drive?

blocks.h: Great advice, but you still drive
blocks.body: A sat nav predicts arrival time, warns of jams and suggests routes based on other drivers' journeys. It is brilliant, but the driver decides, checks the road signs and still talks to the passengers. If the map data is out of date, it will confidently send you down a closed road.

blocks.h: Sat nav to AI on a project
head: Sat nav
AI in PRINCE2 Agile

blocks.text: The sat nav never takes the wheel: AI supports, but does not replace, human decisions.

explain.body: AI can help define products and break them into manageable parts, draft user stories from user needs, prioritize backlog items and run automated tests against quality criteria.

test.q: How can AI support the principle 'focus on products'?
options: By forecasting benefits against budgets
By suggesting who should fill each role
By helping define products and draft user stories
By summarizing lessons from earlier projects
test.why: AI helps define and decompose products, draft user stories and prioritize backlogs (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: That supports ensure continued business justification.

explain.body: AI can help leaders understand the complexity of team relationships, spot individual strengths and track how workload is spread.

test.q: How can AI support leading a project team?
options: By deciding which members leave the team
By setting the team's values for it
By running retrospectives in place of the coach
By revealing relationships, strengths and workload
test.why: AI can help teams understand relationships, strengths and workload distribution (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: Staffing decisions stay with accountable people.
whyNot.1: Values and norms are agreed by the team itself.
whyNot.2: Facilitation stays with the team coach.

explain.body: AI-powered automated testing checks that each product meets its quality specifications, so issues are found early and the team keeps improving.

test.q: Which use of AI mainly supports checking products against their quality specifications?
options: A project chatbot for common questions
AI-powered automated testing
Predictive cost forecasting
Analysis of gaps in role cover
test.why: Automated testing tools powered by AI check that each product meets its quality specifications (15.4.1).

whyNot.3: Role gap analysis supports defined roles.

explain.body: AI output is reviewed by the accountable role before anything is decided, because AI supports rather than replaces human decision-making, and it is only as good as its data.

test.q: Why should people review AI output before decisions are taken on a PRINCE2 Agile project?
options: AI supports human decision-making but does not replace it
AI tools cannot work with real-time project data feeds
PRINCE2 Agile forbids AI in project governance
AI cannot help prioritize backlog items
test.why: AI supports but does not remove human decision-making (15.4.2); the accountable roles decide.

whyNot.1: AI forecasts use historical and real-time data.
whyNot.2: The book describes how AI can support the principles, including governance-related ones.
whyNot.3: AI can help prioritize backlog items (15.4.1).
